findings.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:19 evaluates queued = timezone.now() at module import, causing instances without an explicit timestamp to record the import time instead of their creation time; use field(default_factory=timezone.now).

goldens.comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.
to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:19 evaluates queued = timezone.now() at module import, causing instances without an explicit timestamp to record the import time instead of their creation time; use field(default_factory=timezone.now).
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: the timezone.now() default value is evaluated once at class/module definition time rather than at instance creation time. The golden comment says it's evaluated 'at class definition time' while the candidate says 'at module import', but these refer to the same underlying problem - the datetime is computed once and shared across all instances. Both correctly identify that this causes all objects to share the same timestamp instead of getting their own creation time. The candidate also suggests the correct fix (default_factory).
